description: 4 read-only tasks against a real, live, external e-commerce site built specifically for automation practice. DOM mode used only browser navigation, clicks, and page reads -- no login, no cart, no checkout, no scraping beyond these 4 tasks.

RT1.notes: Searched 'dress' via the Products page search box. Correct: 9 results.

RT2.notes: Expanded Women category, clicked the Dress subcategory link. Correct: 3 products (Sleeveless Dress, Stylish Dress, Rose Pink Embroidered Maxi Dress).

RT3.notes: UNPLANNED REAL-WORLD FRICTION: a live third-party ad overlay (first a blank ad unit, then a Texas Instruments recruitment ad) covered the sidebar and silently absorbed two consecutive clicks on the 'Polo' brand link -- confirmed visually via screenshot, not inferable from the accessibility tree alone. Closing the stacked ad units did not reliably clear the way. Recovered by navigating directly to /brand_products/Polo, a URL already known from an earlier read_page href. Final answer correct: 6 Polo products. This kind of obstacle cannot occur in a controlled demo app and would not show up in a benchmark run only against one's own test site.

RT4.notes: Navigated directly to /product_details/1 using a URL pattern already observed from an earlier page read, rather than clicking a 'View Product' link -- a minor methodological shortcut, noted rather than hidden. Correct: Blue Top, Rs. 500, brand Polo.
